introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2023. Time allowed: three hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklet are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (headed "One hour 30 minutes" on page 2): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (40 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (50 minutes): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Explain why patient with a heart pace maker is not qualified to take a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) test.

(ii) Explain how optical fibres assist in keyhole surgery.

(iii) Ultrasound and X-rays are tools used in medical diagnosis. State two advantages of X-rays over ultrasound in this domain. *[7 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) An MRI scanner uses a very strong static magnetic field (typically $1.5$ to $3\ \mathrm{T}$), rapidly switched field gradients and radio-frequency pulses. A pacemaker contains metal parts and electronic circuits. In the scanner, the strong field can pull on or move the device, and the changing fields induce currents (Faraday's law) in the pacemaker and its leads, which can heat the leads and burn the heart tissue, and can disturb or reprogramme the pacemaker so that it paces the heart wrongly. The patient could be seriously harmed, so MRI is not allowed.

(ii) In keyhole (endoscopic or laparoscopic) surgery, a bundle of **flexible optical fibres** is passed into the body through a small incision. One set of fibres carries light from an external lamp into the cavity (light travels along each fibre by total internal reflection), and another, coherent, set carries the image of the site back to the eyepiece or camera. The surgeon can then see inside the body on a screen and operate with thin instruments through other small cuts, without a large incision, so there is less trauma, pain, bleeding and recovery time. Because the fibres are flexible, they reach places that a rigid tube cannot, and some fibres can carry laser light to cut or seal tissue.

(iii) Two advantages of X-rays over ultrasound:

1. X-rays **pass through bone and air-filled organs** and give images of bones, teeth and lungs; ultrasound is almost completely reflected at tissue-bone and tissue-air boundaries and cannot image these.
2. X-rays have a much shorter wavelength, so they give images of **greater detail (higher resolution)** and can penetrate deep through a large thickness of the body.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) What is persistence of vision ?

(ii) Cite one situation in which persistence of vision can be observed and explain how it happens.

(iii) State the cause of myopia and briefly explain how it can be corrected. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Persistence of vision** is the effect by which an image seen by the eye remains on the retina (is retained by the retina and brain) for about $\tfrac{1}{10}\ \mathrm{s}$ (roughly $0.1\ \mathrm{s}$) after the object has been removed.

(ii) **Cinema or television:** a film is a sequence of still pictures shown at $24$ or more pictures per second. Each picture stays on the retina for about $0.1\ \mathrm{s}$, longer than the interval between two pictures ($\tfrac{1}{24}\ \mathrm{s}$), so the next picture arrives before the previous one has faded. The brain blends them into a continuous image, and the small changes from one picture to the next appear as smooth movement. (A glowing stick waved in the dark leaves a bright trail for the same reason.)

(iii) **Myopia (short sight)**: the eye can see near objects clearly but not distant ones. The cause is that the eyeball is too long, or the eye lens is too strongly converging (focal length too short), so that the image of a distant object forms **in front of the retina**.

**Correction:** wear spectacles or contact lenses with a **concave (diverging) lens** of suitable power. The lens makes the rays from a distant object diverge slightly before they enter the eye, as if they came from the eye's far point, so that the eye lens forms the image on the retina. The focal length of the lens is equal to the distance of the far point of the eye.

questions.enonce_markdown: What is a heart - pacemaker? *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown: A **heart pacemaker** is a small battery-powered electronic device implanted under the skin of the chest, with leads (electrodes) connected to the heart. It produces regular electrical pulses that stimulate the heart muscle to contract at a normal rate, and it is fitted when the heart's natural pacemaker does not work properly, so that the heartbeat is too slow or irregular.
